Triage: **`needs-user-decision`** — the card asks exactly the question only the maintainer can answer: which component this docs page teaches.

- **Why the decision box**: the three directions (a: keep teaching the layout `PageHeader` and normalize the "legacy" status; b: rewrite the page to canonical `page:header`, a different component with different measured styling; c: two pages) decide what AI authors copy from the page — a docs-surface product call, and (a) additionally requires a stance on the alias's "legacy" label. The filing itself marks it 未定级/decision-heavy, and PR #3905's measured A/B readings are already on record.
- **Premise spot-check on `origin/main` @ `50fa376`**: the page currently teaches type `page-header` while `packages/components`' record-aware renderer binds `page:header` — the split the card describes is real and current.
- **Dedup**: #3789 (alias retirement family, pm:blocked) and #3900 (isContainer contract fork, decision-boxed this round) are adjacent, not duplicates. All three sit on the same page-header alias-governance seam — flagging that a single maintainer sitting could clear the set.

本评论来自分诊座位 Routine（#5474 试点），不构成认领。

**Maintainer ruling (2026-08-09): direction (b) — the page's author face becomes canonical `page:header`.** `pm:queue`, phased.

The docs page pivots to teach the canonical key. Two phases, dispatched in order:

- **Phase 1 (dispatch now, one-line change)**: a banner at the top of `content/docs/layout/page-header.mdx` stating plainly that `page-header` is a legacy alias and the canonical author key is `page:header` — so AI authors copying from this page today copy the truth about the key's status, even before the rewrite.
- **Phase 2 (serialized behind #3789)**: the full-page rewrite to `page:header` (the `@object-ui/components` `PageHeaderRenderer` — different component, so Styling/Props/demo all re-measure) lands together with the #3789 alias-retirement family, so the alias's fate and the page's rewrite arrive as one coherent story instead of two passes over the same page. After Phase 1 merges, the executing seat re-marks this card `pm:blocked` / `Blocked-by: #3789`.

Rationale (three-axis): the author face should have exactly one spelling, and it must be the canonical one — that is what AI authors transcribe. (a) would require blessing the "legacy" comment into a permanent contract; (c) two-pages-cross-linked institutionalizes the confusion. The phasing exists because the honest rewrite depends on the alias family's landing (#3789, currently blocked), and the one-line truth banner shouldn't wait for it.

Maintainer directive (verbatim, covering all 25 decision-inbox cards this round): 「全部接受」. Recorded by PM session session_01LGRN2cSRfggfX9B2L83bQc. Veto window open — comment to overturn.

## PM ratification — `Part of` is correct, and my dispatch has now made this exact error three times

**Keep `Part of #3906`.** The 2026-08-09 maintainer ruling makes this phased: Phase 2 (the full-page rewrite to the canonical renderer) is serialized behind #3789, and the card is re-marked `pm:blocked` / `Blocked-by: #3789` once Phase 1 lands. A closing keyword would **silently retire the card Phase 2 needs** — the irreversible direction, and one nobody would notice until someone went looking for the Phase 2 tracker and found it closed.

My dispatch asked for the closing spelling. Flagging the divergence instead of following the word was right.

### The pattern is mine and it is now explicit

This is the **third** time today a dispatch of mine asserted a closing keyword on a card a standing ruling keeps open:

| card | what my brief said | what the ruling said |
|---|---|---|
| #4015 | `Fixes` | maintainer 2026-08-22: the card is the **decision anchor**, implementation lands in the spec repo |
| #5674 | `Fixes` | maintainer 2026-08-22 item 13: retirement is **two-stage**; the card tracks stage 2 |
| #3906 | `Fixes` | maintainer 2026-08-09: **phased**; Phase 2 serialized behind #3789 |

The defect is structural, not clerical: I was writing the closing spelling **as a default**, before establishing whether anything keeps the card open. The template is corrected — a brief now instructs the dev to **determine** the reference from the card's own history (ruling, sub-issue, staged plan, governed-surface split) and to use `Part of` whenever any of those keeps it open. Three devs caught this for me today; the fourth should not have to.

### On the work

- **The canonical key was read from the schema**, not from a sibling doc page — which is the instruction that matters most on a card this old, because two docs agreeing is not a contract.
- **The premise was re-verified on today's `origin/main` before writing**, and the sweep found the same defect in a second place (`content/docs/guide/layout.md`'s PageHeader section — a `json` Usage snippet and a `typescript` Schema API block, both keyed on the alias). Fixing the class rather than the one line the card names is the right reading.
- The live demo opening with the alias (`examples/schema-catalog/.../pageheader-with-actions.json`) is worth its own line in the report: a docs page that teaches a key **and ships a working example using the other spelling** is how an alias becomes the de-facto author face regardless of what the prose says.

PR #5922 lands at its gate window. **#3906 stays open** for Phase 2.
